paper_metadata.title: Federated Learning in Quantum Computing for Privacy-Preserving and Distributed Quantum Model Training

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical privacy-preserving federated learning framework (PQFL) for distributed training of parameterized quantum models with secure aggregation and differential privacy; evaluated against centralized QML and PQFL variants.

algorithm.variant: Privacy-Preserving Quantum Federated Learning (PQFL) with Quantum Homomorphic Encryption (QHE) and Quantum Differential Privacy (QDP)
algorithm.optimizer: SGD or Adam (examples mentioned; exact optimizer not specified)

problem_formulation.encoding_method: angle_encoding or amplitude_encoding (examples mentioned; exact method not specified)
problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features x_k are encoded into quantum states |psi_k> via a feature encoding circuit E(x_k); no explicit qubit-to-feature mapping given.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize local loss L_i(theta_i^t) = (1/m_i) * sum_k (y_k - y_hat_k)^2 for binary classification-style training; global model updated by averaging client deltas.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Secure aggregation via QHE; privacy protection via QDP noise injection before encryption.

problem_instance.description: Distributed training of local parameterized quantum circuits across multiple clients in a federated setting; evaluated on generic quantum ML tasks and discussed for privacy-sensitive domains including healthcare, genomics, and finance.

dataset_specification.description: No specific dataset, ticker symbols, date range, or benchmark are reported; local client datasets D_i are described abstractly as labeled quantum examples.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Each client encodes local samples into quantum states and computes gradients via the parameter-shift rule; no explicit preprocessing pipeline reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Hybrid quantum-classical simulations comparing centralized QML, PQFL without QDP, and PQFL with QDP; metrics reported include accuracy, privacy loss epsilon, communication overhead, and qubit utilization.

noise_model.noise_description: QDP noise injection; quantum Gaussian noise and optional depolarizing/Pauli noise channels

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Local client-side training of parameterized quantum circuits; gradients computed with parameter-shift rule; local optimizer update before encryption.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Encrypted aggregation at server; decryption performed locally by clients; global parameters updated by averaging decrypted noisy deltas.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit computational speedup or runtime advantage claim is reported; the paper focuses on privacy-preserving distributed training and reports accuracy/privacy/communication metrics.
